If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to compensate for bearish bias.  
In mid-horizon (days 8–15), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day to reflect sentiment reversal.  
In late-horizon (days 16–30), if sentiment remains negative, apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast, especially if true price has already fallen below 70% of initial forecast.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day in late horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day in late horizon to avoid underestimating downside risk.
